projects.title: Employee Sports Benefits Data Platform
projects.scenario: Case study set by the programme.

sections.label: Problem
sections.text: In the case study, a company wanted to test the feasibility of two employee benefits and to estimate their financial impact.

sections.label: Approach
sections.text: An end-to-end pipeline that loads and validates HR and activity data, orchestrates the workflow, posts activities to Slack and presents indicators on a dashboard.

sections.label: Technical implementation
sections.text: Airflow DAGs orchestrate the workflow, with a PostgreSQL store, Superset dashboards and numbered Bash scripts as a manual fallback, all containerised with Docker Compose. The data are simulated employee and activity data (161 employees).

sections.label: Validation
sections.text: Data-quality checks run in the pipeline, and commute distances are validated with the Google Maps Distance Matrix API.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.text: A proof of concept; activity data is simulated, not read from a live service.

figures.alt: Stacked bar chart of the combined financial impact in euros under three wellness scenarios (30, 50 and 70 per cent), split into bonus cost and wellness cost.
figures.caption: Combined financial impact of the two benefits under three wellness scenarios, from the financial impact notebook.

projects.title: Healthcare Data Migration Pipeline
projects.scenario: Case study set by the programme.

sections.label: Problem
sections.text: In the case study, a healthcare provider with scalability problems needed its medical records migrated from a CSV file to MongoDB.

sections.label: Approach
sections.text: A seven-step ETL workflow with automated cleaning and integrity testing, a containerised deployment, and a written study of cloud deployment options on AWS.

sections.label: Technical implementation
sections.text: Name standardisation and duplicate removal, and memory use reduced by 21% through categorical and datetime types. Built with Python, pandas, PyMongo, MongoDB, Docker, pytest and Poetry.

sections.label: Validation
sections.text: Five integrity tests pass under pytest. 54,966 medical records remain after cleaning (55,500 in the source file).

sections.label: Outcome
sections.text: A Docker Compose deployment of MongoDB with a web interface for the database, and an AWS comparison of DocumentDB, Atlas, EC2 and ECS.

figures.alt: Flow diagram of the migration pipeline: load the raw CSV (55,500 rows), clean the data, connect to MongoDB, load 54,966 cleaned rows, bulk insert, validate integrity and finish.
figures.caption: ETL pipeline flow, from the repository documentation.

figures.alt: Diagram of the Docker infrastructure: a Python migration container and a Mongo Express container connect over a shared network to a MongoDB 8.2 container with a mounted data volume.
figures.caption: Docker infrastructure, from the repository documentation.

projects.title: RAG Chatbot for Cultural Event Recommendations
projects.scenario: Case study set by the programme.

sections.label: Problem
sections.text: Recommending cultural events in Paris so that answers are grounded in real listings rather than in the general knowledge of a language model.

sections.label: Approach
sections.text: A retrieval-augmented generation proof of concept using live Open Agenda data. Events are fetched from the Open Agenda API, cleaned and filtered to the past 12 months in the Paris region, with one text chunk per event, embedded and indexed for similarity search.

sections.label: Technical implementation
sections.text: A single LangChain chain serves both the Streamlit chatbot and the evaluation, with Mistral AI and FAISS. Built with Python, LangChain, Mistral AI, FAISS, Streamlit, RAGAS, pytest and Poetry.

sections.label: Validation
sections.text: Evaluation with RAGAS on 30 questions, and 25 automated pytest tests.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.text: A proof of concept: single-turn, one data source, manual rebuilds.

figures.alt: Flow diagram of the RAG pipeline: Open Agenda events, cleaning, mistral-embed embedding, a FAISS index and Mistral generation.
figures.caption: RAG pipeline from event data to answer generation, from the repository notebooks.

projects.title: EduGlobe Insights: Education Data Analysis
projects.scenario: Case study set by the programme.

sections.label: Problem
sections.text: Judging whether World Bank EdStats data can support the international expansion of an online education service for high school and university learners.

sections.label: Approach
sections.text: Exploration, cleaning and analysis of the five EdStats tables (indicator values, series catalogue, country metadata, country-series links, footnotes), downloaded separately from the World Bank and not included in the repository.

sections.label: Technical implementation
sections.text: Three Jupyter notebooks, using pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly and SciPy.

sections.label: Validation
sections.text: The indicators are assessed for relevance, completeness and reliability.

figures.alt: Line chart of the percentage of missing values by year from 1970 to 2100, with the period 1995 to 2015 marked as the optimal period for analysis and later years shown as projections.
figures.caption: Share of missing values by year in the education indicators, from the analysis notebook.
